messages.subject: barrier model specification and interpretation
parts:
Hi all,
I am working through a gamma hurdle model with a spatial barrier and wanted to ensure that my specification of the model and interpretation of the output was correct. My response in the model (gamma portion) is catch-per-effort and I have 2 categorical covariates, gear (2 levels; EF and DT) and habitat (3 levels; Trib, MC, and SC) in my model. I have created the model as follows:

# create the gamma response
SVC2$pos <- ifelse(SVC2$CPUE_Ped_Hr > 0, SVC2$CPUE_Ped_Hr, NA)

# create the model matrix
Xm <- model.matrix(~ fGear + fHabitat, data = SVC2)
X <- data.frame(fGearDT = Xm[, 2],
                fHabitatMC = Xm[, 3],
                fHabitatSC = Xm[, 4])

# create the stack including the spatial random field
stack.gamma9 <- inla.stack(tag = 'GammaFit9',
                           data = list(pos = SVC2$pos),
                           A = list(1, 1, 1, A2),
                           effects = list(Intercept = rep(1, N),
                                          X = X,
                                          Site = SVC2$Site,
                                          w = w2.index))

# write the formula
fgamma9 <- formula(pos ~ -1 + Intercept + fGearEF + fHabitatSC + fHabitatTrib +
                     f(Site, model = 'iid') + f(w, model = spde2))

# run the model
system.time(
barrier.g <- inla(fgamma9,
                  family = 'gamma',
                  data = inla.stack.data(stack.gamma9),
                  control.compute = list(dic = T,
                                         waic = T),
                  control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A(stack.gamma9),
                                           link = 1))
)

summary(barrier.g)

(Posterior marginals needs also 'control.compute=list(return.marginals.predictor=TRUE)')

My questions are:
1) Is including the random effects of site (includes multiple sampling locations) and the spatial component in the same model valid, or will these random effects be confounded?

2) I am interpreting the fixed effects as indicating that there is a negative effect of gear = EF relative to gear = DT but the potential effects of habitat are unimportant (95% credible intervals overlap 0), but I'm not sure how to interpret the hyperparameters. I've been primarily using the Zuur et al. 2018 book (GAM and zero-inflated models) to guide my analysis and haven't found a concise explanation for the interpretation of these values. Guidance is appreciated.

3) Is there a way to understand the potential site or spatial effects on the gear differences? Essentially, this would be examining an interaction among gear and site/space to determine if the relationship among gears changes throughout the study area.

4) What is the interpretation of the spatial random field (obtained using barrier.g$summary.random$w$mean; figure attached axes are in UTM/1000) and is there a way to understand the magnitude of the differences? Based on my reading, I would interpret this as indicating that areas in red have relatively high catch-per-effort (regardless of gear) and areas in blue have relatively low catch-per effort but the magnitude of the differences is unclear.

5) Is there another book/resource that you would recommend as a guide? I have seen several on the R-INLA website but I'm not sure which might be most appropriate for understanding the interpretation of the output from this type of analysis.

I know that that is a lot of questions but I really appreciate any help or guidance.
Thanks,
Ben

messages.author: 74f2e6fef4c447fd
messages.subject: Re: barrier model specification and interpretation
parts:
Hi Ben,

(1) Having the random site effect plus the spatial field seems fine to me. You can think of the field as a spatially smoothed intercept and the random site effect as describing the local deviation around the field.
(2a) "negative effect of gear = EF relative to gear = DT"  That seems right to me.  
(2b) "the potential effects of habitat are unimportant" That's what the contrasts suggest, but another way to test that is to run another model without any habitat effects and compare WAIC.
(2c) The hyperparameter summaries tell you how much variation is accounted for by the different model components. Variation is expressed as precision (1/variance). Precision for Gamma obs = 1.86 is another way of saying that the raw residual in the model has an SD of sqrt(1/1.86)) = 0.73. Precision for site = 488 is like saying the site effect has a SD of sqrt(1/488) = 0.05, which is small compared to raw residual (0.73). One of the theta1 and theta2 describes the variation explained by the spatial field and the other describes the range of the spatial decay function (where the spatial correlation coefficient decreases to around 0.1). I don't remember which is which. What are your spatial units? Meters? Kilometers? Not sure why theta1 is a negative number.
(3) There is a way to see if the gear effects vary across space. It is called a spatially varying coefficient model. The newest versions of INLA and inlabru have a vignette for how to build an SVC model.
(4) I think you have the interpretation of the field correct? The spatial field is a smooth adjustment to the global intercept, yes? As for magnitude, think about any transformations needed. Does the gamma model use a log link?
(5) There are several great references. In many cases the authors are kind enough to provide an accessible ebook. For example: https://becarioprecario.bitbucket.io/spde-gitbook/ and https://becarioprecario.bitbucket.io/inla-gitbook/index.html. 

Best,
Tim
